direction: Improve the insertion-move scoring so the guided insertion builds a tour that needs fewer/cheaper 2-opt repairs: score each candidate insertion by its immediate cost delta plus a k-nearest-neighbor-based lookahead penalty on the two edges it creates, and restrict the 2-opt repair to neighbor-induced pairs with a best-improvement first-improvement hybrid and a deterministic don't-look-bit skip list.

operations.mechanism: KB method-tsp-two-opt documents the exact delta formula dist(a,c)+dist(b,d)-dist(a,b)-dist(c,d) for Croes-style 2-opt restricted to a k-nearest geometric graph, with a step cap that fits the 500 ms budget; it also warns that neighbor-restricted repair is a post-construct operator, which is why the change keeps construct (guided insertion via score_insertion_move) separate from repair and why insertion scoring gets a 2-opt-awareness lookahead penalty rather than absorbing the 2-opt search. Insertion construction guidance comes from the TSPTW generalized insertion entry (cheapest-insertion with reoptimization) and improved-NN entry (deterministic greedy ordering for reproducibility). Round 1 measured 10.2 ms mean solve time against a 500 ms budget, so roughly 50x headroom exists; spending it on more 2-opt sweeps with don't-look bits should convert to objective reduction rather than exhaust. Weakest regimes are size-sensitive (rel gap ~-15% at n=50 and n=100), so the plan emphasizes repair completeness on small/medium instances where extra sweeps are cheapest.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Under a 500 ms budget on dev_24 (n=50/100/200, mean objective ~84740), a neighbor-restricted best-improvement 2-opt with don't-look bits plus a lookahead-weighted insertion score (score_insertion_move penalizing long created edges) yields a lower mean tour cost than round 1's pure greedy-cheapest insertion + full-scan 2-opt, because the O(n) full neighborhood scan is replaced by O(n*k) neighbor pairs, freeing budget for more repair rounds and producing a better starting tour.
